build.goal: Turn a pasted to-do list with rough durations into a realistic plan for the hours available today, ordered by importance, and clearly state what won't fit.
build.instructions:
App name for the person: Fits In Today Planner

What success looks like: After pasting a list and saying "I have 4 hours", the user gets a plan in pasted order whose total stays within 4 hours, plus a short list of the items left out and the time each needs.

How the person will use it:
- User opens Alpha and runs the planner. -> It asks for the to-do list and the hours available today.
- User pastes the list with rough times and says how many hours they have. -> Each line is read as an item with a duration; missing durations are estimated and marked as estimates.
- The planner keeps the pasted order and fills the available hours. -> An ordered plan with each item's time and a running total that does not exceed the hours given.
- User reads the leftovers. -> A "won't fit today" list with each item, the time it needs, and the total time short.
- User corrects a time or reorders lines and runs it again. -> A fresh plan reflecting the correction; nothing from the previous run is carried over.

What it does:
- action read_list: Takes the pasted text and the hours available. Reads one item per line, keeps the pasted order as the importance order, and pulls out the rough duration in common formats (90m, 1.5h, 1:30). Items with no duration get an estimate, clearly marked as an estimate the user can correct. (inputs: pasted to-do text, hours available today; outputs: ordered list of items with name, duration, estimated flag)
- action fit_plan: Goes down the list in pasted order and adds each item while the running total stays within the available hours. An item longer than the time remaining is kept whole and set aside for "won't fit"; the planner carries on down the list so smaller items can still use the gap. (inputs: ordered list of items with durations, hours available today; outputs: ordered plan with running totals, leftover items with durations)
- action report_plan: Writes the plan back in the conversation: items in order with their times and the total used against the hours available, then a short "won't fit today" list with the time each leftover needs and the total time short. (inputs: ordered plan, leftover items; outputs: plan text with won't-fit list)

Constraints:
- The planned total never exceeds the hours the user says they have.
- Items are ordered exactly as pasted; the planner never reorders them.
- Every pasted item appears either in the plan or in the won't-fit list; none are dropped silently.
- No item is split into a partial block.
- Estimated durations are always labelled as estimates.
- Nothing is stored between runs.

Agreed assumptions:
- Importance = the order you paste them in; the first line is the most important.
- Output is the order with durations and a running total; no clock times, so no start time needed.
- An item longer than the time left goes whole into "won't fit"; smaller items behind it can still fill the gap.
- Times are read from common formats (90m, 1.5h, 1:30); missing ones get a labelled estimate.
- No breaks or buffer added unless you ask.
- Saving past plans, priority labels, or splitting long tasks can be added later.

PLAN.md is what Alpha will check. Where it names an action, input, collection, field or label differently from the notes above, use PLAN.md's name.

This App has no custom screen: leave ui out of app.yaml. People run its actions from Alpha's own view, so give every action a clear title and description.

- `app.yaml` — the exact platform values, `capabilities: [records]` with one collection `plans` declared but never written (each run plans afresh, so it stays empty), no `ui` block, and three clearly titled actions runnable from Alpha's own view (`manual`, `assistant`).

I covered the same ground by running the logic through `python -m unittest` and hand-checking that each handler's parameters match its `input_schema` properties, with every no-default parameter listed as required; `app.yaml` indentation and plain-scalar colons were reviewed by reading the file.
